statement.p: Let \mathbf{F}(x,y,z)=z\tan(y^2)\mathbf{i} + z^3\ln(x^2+1)\mathbf{j} + 4\mathbf{k}. Use the Divergence Theorem to find the flux of \mathbf{F} across the part of the paraboloid x^2+y^2+z=2 that lies above the plane z=1 and is oriented upwards.

static.solution: S_2 = S\cup S_1, where S is the part of the paraboloid x^2+y^2+z=2) that lies above the plan \(z=1, and S_1 is the disk x^2+y^2=1 on the plane =1 downward, and we then apply the Divergence Theorem. Since the disk S_1 is oriented downward, its unit normal vector is \mathbf{n} = -\mathbf{k} and \mathbf{F} \cdot (-\mathbf{k}) = -4 z = -4 on S_1. So \int\int_{S_1} \mathbf{F} \cdot \ d \mathbf{S} = \int\int_{S_1} \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \ dS = \int\int_{S_1} (-4) \ dS = -4 A(S_1) = -4\pi. Let E be the region bounded by S_2. Then \int\int_{S_2} \mathbf{F} \cdot \ d \mathbf{S} = \int \int \int_E {\rm div } \mathbf{F} \ dV = \int\int\int_E 4 \ dV = 4\int_0^{1}\int_0^{2\pi}\int_1^{2-r^2} r \ dz \ d\theta \ dr = 4\int_0^{1}\int_0^{2\pi} (1 r - r^3) \ d\theta \ dr = 8 \pi\int_0^{1} (1 r - r^3)\ dr = 8\pi(\frac 1 2 1 - \frac 1 4 1) = 2\pi. Thus the flux of \mathbf{F} across S is \int\int_S \mathbf{F}\cdot \ d \mathbf{S}\ = \int\int_{S_2} \mathbf{F}\cdot \ d \mathbf{S}\ - \int\int_{S_1} \mathbf{F}\cdot \ d \mathbf{S}\ = 2\pi + 4\pi = 6\pi.
